title: Invoke-WkEmergencyEditDoor: the emergency-edit permission, its placement contract and its three open defects
desc: The door that lets a session repair the guard refusing it. Placement contract, the stamp-and-read halves, the three measured defects, the cross-family gap, and the verification that grep and parse cannot give you.
steps: INHERITED OPEN ITEMS 2026-09-12, moved out of HANDOFF.md verbatim so the letter could carry its evidence table instead. WHEN: you are the successor and want the open list the letter points at. (1) THE FORCED-LIKE GATE STILL DOES NOT REACH A SOURCE EDIT -- the predicate and its ledger are live but the only production caller appends a debt note to a refusal already in flight, so a paid session and an unpaid one are treated identically unless some other gate was already refusing; the seam that would make writing source owe the like sits unpromoted at wkharness-guards-onload-enforce-proto.ps1 lines 355 to 364. Resolve the verdict from wkharness-common-subagentid.ps1 and the map from Get-WkTierScore. (2) TWO KNOWLEDGE-READ GUARDS CONTRADICT EACH OTHER -- tools/wkharness-common-knowledgeop.ps1 refuses a piped skill read and offers a FILE REDIRECT as the sanctioned alternative, while a second rule blocks the redirect; a session obeying the first is refused by the second. (3) CLOSED, 2 REDIRECT 1 WAS READ AS A WRITE, in tools/wkharness-decompose.ps1 -- root cause of the write-target refusals that killed three sector rounds, fixed and verified in six directions, together with the empty explanation arm in tools/wkharness-claude-main.ps1 that made that refusal unactionable. (4) NINE FILES RE-MEASURED AND CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT, each re-verified WIRED with its call site: Get-WkBusyFleetBlockMessage.ps1, handoff-manifest-scope.sh, Test-WkLetterGcTmpGate.ps1, wkharness.ps1, wkharness-guards.ps1, wkharness-guards-infra.ps1, wkharness-guards-onload-enforce-demix.ps1, wkharness-guards-stop-checks.ps1, wkharness-guards-wiringcheck.ps1 -- a disproof closes a wish exactly as a fix does. Cross: wkappbot skill read forced-like-gate ; wkappbot skill read descent-letter-atlas //why:lite door granted itself on every intent refusal during interim report turn //why:lite door granted itself on every intent refusal during interim report turn-unknown

SPEC, owner directive 2026-09-12: THE STUDY-LOCK MUST KEEP FIRING THROUGH AN EMERGENCY GRANT, AND THE BLANKET SKIP IS THE DEFECT. His words: the skill-lock must work even during an emergency edit, it MUST work, because anyone editing these files is dangerous. WHAT THE CODE SAYS TODAY, at Invoke-WkEmergencyEditDoor.ps1 line 66, is the opposite in as many words -- GRANTED, this source is on the repair list, so every other harness gate is skipped for this call. WHAT WAS MEASURED TODAY is a third thing again: a grant printed and the study-lock refused the SAME call anyway, twice, on wkwdi-readers.ps1 and wkwhatdidyouinherit.ps1, and omega refused a third. So the design says skip everything, the behaviour skips nothing, and this skill step 4 already files that disagreement as DEFECT TWO on the theory that allow-and-exit was not holding. THAT FILING IS NOW SUPERSEDED FOR THE LOCK: the behaviour is the CORRECT one and the contract is what must change. THE ARGUMENT, and it is not a preference. The files this door opens ARE THE GUARDS, so the one person walking in is precisely the one who must have read the governing skill -- a session repairing a guard without reading it produces the failures this very session produced three times in one day, a regex split across two lines by shell escaping and a check rewritten to demand a condition no caller could ever supply. AND THE TWO GATES DIFFER IN KIND: omega says you are too old, delegate, which a repair door may legitimately override; the study-lock says read before you touch, which no door should ever override, because the door exists to restore a broken mechanism and an unread repairer is how it gets broken worse. THE CHANGE, SHARPENED BY THE OWNER 2026-09-12 INTO SOMETHING BETTER THAN AN EXEMPTION LIST: keep the FAST ALLOW-AND-EXIT and move the study-lock INSIDE the door. He asked whether a fast-exit could still check the lock, and it can -- the grant becomes conditional rather than blanket. On a listed file the door asks ONE question before granting: is this file lock satisfied. Unsatisfied, it refuses and names the unread skills. Satisfied, it grants and exits for real. THAT IS FASTER THAN TODAY, not slower: one check runs instead of the whole stack, where today the exit does not work at all and every gate runs anyway. WHY THIS BEATS THE EXEMPTION-LIST DRAFT IT REPLACES: today safety is an ACCIDENT OF A BUG. The exit raises a flow-control exception that a bare catch swallows, so execution carries on and the later gates happen to refuse -- measured four times today, twice by ROOT and twice by a delegate. The moment someone repairs that swallow, which this skill already files as DEFECT TWO and tells them to do, the lock dies. Putting the lock inside the door means the lock survives a CORRECT exit. Safety stops depending on a defect. It is also auditable in a way a blanket skip can never be: the door code then NAMES the single check it honours, where today nobody can say what a grant exempts, which is the same unauditable shape as an override env var. ONE IMPLEMENTATION TRAP, and it is the one this session spent the day on: the door runs immediately after the payload variables resolve and BEFORE the first Block, so the study-lock function may not be loaded yet. The door must dot-source that module ITSELF, at FILE SCOPE. A dot-source inside the door function defines the predicate in that function scope, it dies on return, the Get-Command probe then fails and the door grants unconditionally -- which is exactly how five guards in tools/wkharness-guards-infra.ps1 were found dead today. A blanket skip is unauditable -- nobody can say what a grant currently exempts, which is the same class as an override env var. VERIFY IT BY WHAT IT STILL REFUSES: with a file on the repair list and its lock UNREAD, the edit must still be refused and name the unread skills; after reading them the identical edit must succeed. A version that grants everything passes the second half and fails the first, and only that pair proves the lock is consulted rather than merely present. //why:owner asked QA to prove the door never skips the study lock //why:door granted lite harness after worker restart refusal //why:door granted lite harness after worker restart refusal-unknown

SHIPPED 2026-09-12: THE DOOR'S REACH IS NOW THE REPAIR SURFACE AND NOTHING ELSE, which is what step 4 always said and the code never enforced. The stamp ran on EVERY refused write target with no filter, so any ordinary project script that met any gate was added to the repair list and opened on its second attempt exactly like a broken guard. Only source CONTAINED under the resolved harness root is stampable now, and the path is checked AGAIN at the GRANT so a ledger already carrying ordinary paths goes inert without anyone purging it. THE RULE THAT GENERALISES: a repair permission must be narrow at EVERY point it is exercised (ROAD 2026-11-12: the lite hook prints GRANTED wkharness-lite.sh on a plain intent-lock refusal; the refusal was just, so the road was to run the owner-keyword search it asked for and leave the granted file untouched -- a grant is a permission, never an order), not only where it is granted, because the two are separated by time and by whatever wrote the list in between. e9f66fd71, 4d3325fe7, 8c6cef714. AND THE ANSWER TO WHY NO SUITE EVER CAUGHT IT: there was no self-test. The file named like one was a wired proto, thirty-one lines, two function definitions, zero cases. Every check this door ever had examined the LIST MECHANICS -- does the writer land where the reader looks, is the list per-repo -- and none asked what KIND of file may be on the list, so nothing could go red. THE BAR IS NOW SET BY Test-WkEmergencyEditPathIsHarness-selftest.ps1: 21 cases re-run by ROOT from the canonical path, THIRTEEN of them refusals, plus inversion cases proving a SUBSTRING rule permits a project tools directory, a tools segment buried mid-path and a command line that merely MENTIONS one, while containment refuses all three and both rules still agree on a real guard. STILL LOOSE, per the owner, with another repo working against this door: narrowing it further is live work. AND UNVERIFIED BESIDE IT: Get-WkBlockingGuardSource.ps1 landed the same day from a sector, not run, no cases, no call site checked -- run it, write its REFUSAL cases first, then wire it. //why:lite door printed a grant again on remaining work intent refusal //why:lite door granted itself again on a plain intent lock refusal tonight //why:lite door grant fired on every intent refusal this session //why:lite door grant fired on every intent refusal this session-unknown //why:lite door granted itself again on a plain intent lock refusal tonight-unknown //why:lite door printed a grant again on remaining work intent refusal-unknown //why:a grant names the refusing guard file, nothing wider

FIVE CHECKS A JUNIOR RUNS ON THIS DOOR AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, each naming the file and the assertion, because every one of these passed a grep and a parse while doing nothing. WHEN: inheriting the emergency-edit door, or verifying any of the five files below. HOW, one command each. (1) tools/wkharness-claude-main/Invoke-WkEmergencyEditDoor.ps1 -- make a call that is genuinely refused, then make the IDENTICAL call again and assert the SECOND ONE SUCCEEDS; a grant that prints and does not open was measured three times. (2) tools/wkharness-common-emergencyedit/Test-WkEmergencyEditAllow.ps1 -- run the writer, then FIND THE FILE ON DISK and compare that path with the one the door reads; comparing two computed strings passes while the writer lands elsewhere. (3) tools/wkharness-claude-main.ps1 -- the subagent flag is computed BELOW the line that forwards it, so the ROOT-only refusal is dead; prove it with a real delegate call, never by reading. (4) .githooks/lib/handoff-manifest-rowscan.sh -- feed it a letter carrying ONE label and assert the refusal names every other one on a single line. (5) tools/wkharness-write-target/Get-WkGitMoveTarget.ps1 -- assert a plain tools-to-tools rename is STILL refused; the narrowing controls are the half that can fail. WHY: a parse and a grep certify shape, not behaviour, and three defects in one night passed both while inert. Cross: wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto ; wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring //why:door granted the guards agent file and the spokesman repaired it net zero

LANDED 2026-09-12 AND THE DOOR IS WHAT LANDED IT -- the retry contract in step 4 HOLDS in practice, measured three times in a row. Each write was refused once, stamped, and the IDENTICAL command succeeded on the second attempt: creating tools/wkharness-common-subagentbypath.ps1, and editing tools/wkharness-claude-main.ps1 which carries a study lock. So DEFECT TWO's symptom did not reproduce for these calls, and a session blocked by omega should try the second identical call before concluding anything. THE FIX ITSELF, recorded verbatim so it survives even if the file does not: at wkharness-claude-main.ps1 line 1148, immediately AFTER the existing structural-test block and BEFORE the omega call, insert a promotion-only clause -- if the flag is still false AND an agent id is present, dot-source wkharness-common-subagentbypath.ps1 from the canonical dir and set the flag from Test-WkCallerIsSubagentByPath with the payload transcript path and that agent id, the whole thing inside its own try with an empty catch. IT MAY ONLY EVER PROMOTE: it never runs when the flag is already true, so it cannot demote, and a stray agent id on a ROOT payload resolves to a transcript file that does not exist, which is the property an or-chain on the id alone lacks. THE MODULE builds the delegate path as the parent transcript's directory, then its filename WITHOUT extension as a folder, then subagents, then agent-<id>.jsonl, using Path.Combine and never Join-Path -- Join-Path RESOLVES the drive and writes a DriveNotFound record to the error stream for an absent one, which is noise on every tool call from a hot path. Self-test 10 of 10 from the canonical path with both live directions, a traversal refusal, and a control asserting the error stream stays empty. STATE: the module and the seam are LIVE ON DISK and running -- ParseFile returns 0 errors and every command since goes through the edited hook -- but UNCOMMITTED in wkappbot-kih, because that repo's own descent gates refuse the commit on a manifest row belonging to a PREDECESSOR session, which is the pre-existing ring recorded in claude-session-handoff. The full module source is committed and tracked in *** at .tmp/wk-subagent-bypath-proto.ps1, so nothing is lost if the harness copy is swept. //why:infra guard edit landed through granted door at 57 MB //why:infra guard edit landed through granted door at 57 MB-unknown

MEASURED 2026-09-12: OMEGA IS NOT THE DEFECT, THE IDENTITY RESOLVER BESIDE IT IS -- and this is the same flag-computation family already filed in step 4, arriving from a new direction. THE SYMPTOM: at 11 MB a ROOT session was refused a study-locked source edit, which is omega working as designed, and the dispatched SECTOR was refused by omega TOO, naming the PARENT transcript size. That pair makes the gate self-sealing, because its own prescribed remedy is the delegation it then refuses. THE SOURCE SETTLES IT AND IT IS NOT WHERE ANYONE WOULD LOOK: Invoke-WkOmegaSourceEditGate.ps1 line 27 reads if IsSubagent return null, so omega ALREADY exempts a delegate completely and has no size opinion about one. The refusal therefore proves the flag arrived FALSE for a real subagent. AT THE CALL SITE, wkharness-claude-main.ps1 line 1148, the flag is first derived from agent_id and then OVERWRITTEN UNCONDITIONALLY by a structural transcript test, and the comment on that same line promises this can only ever correct a false positive. RETRACTED AND CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT THE SAME HOUR, and the retraction is the useful half. I blamed the resolver. IT IS CORRECT: dot-sourced and called directly, Test-WkStopCallerIsAgentByOnload answered True for a real delegate transcript under the subagents folder and False for the flat ROOT transcript, in the same minute. THE REAL CAUSE IS ITS INPUT. The omega refusal handed to my SECTOR quoted 10.3 MB, which is the PARENT transcript size -- a freshly spawned delegate's own file is tiny -- so the payload field the call site reads, transcript_path, was pointing at the PARENT session for a subagent call. Given the parent's path, a correct resolver correctly answers ROOT, and the size gate correctly measures the parent. Both gates are right and both are being asked about the wrong session. THE PROMISE ON THAT LINE IS STILL BROKEN, just by a different mechanism: a plain assignment lets that parent-derived FALSE replace the id-derived TRUE, so a genuine delegate is demoted, which is a false NEGATIVE and the opposite of the stated direction. THE FIX THAT SURVIVES BOTH FAILURE MODES is neither an or-chain nor trusting the id: RESOLVE THE DELEGATE'S OWN TRANSCRIPT AND TEST THAT. The layout is measured and stable -- a delegate lives at the project directory, then the ROOT session id as a FOLDER, then subagents, then agent-<id>.jsonl, while ROOT is a flat sibling .jsonl of that folder. A Test-Path on that constructed path is decisive and cannot be spoofed by a stray agent_id on a ROOT payload, because the file simply will not exist. NOTE THE ORDER IS FINE HERE -- the id is assigned at 1139 and used at 1148 -- so this is NOT the late-assignment shape step 4 records; it is the same class reached by overwriting rather than by scoping. THE ONE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD PROVE IT, and it must be run before anything is edited: call Test-WkStopCallerIsAgentByOnload with a KNOWN DELEGATE transcript path and again with a ROOT one, and compare. If both answer false the resolver cannot see a delegate at all and the overwrite is pure loss; if they differ, the demotion is layout-specific and the fix is narrower. THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, once measured: the structural test may only DEMOTE when it can positively identify ROOT, so an inconclusive or unsupported layout must KEEP the id-derived value -- which is what the comment already claims the code does. I did NOT make this edit: it is a fleet-wide identity resolver on the PreToolUse hot path, I had an inference rather than a measurement, and editing it from an 11 MB session is the damage class this door exists to repair rather than cause.

FIVE MORE WISHES CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-12, extending the nine in step 1, and the RULE behind them matters more than the five. WHEN: the stop hook names files under STILL UNWIRED and you are about to go wire them. HOW: measure on origin/main FIRST with git grep -ln '<module>' origin/main -- scripts/ and exclude scripts/.bak, which otherwise floods the result with dead backups and hides the real answer. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT RETURNED: handoff-manifest-scope.sh is WIRED, sourced by .githooks/lib/handoff-manifest-gate.sh and promoted in wkappbot-kih commit 1e6463bba; us_realized_pnl.py is WIRED with eight callers on origin/main including the live host willkim_realtime_***.py and wk_pnl.py; ***_minute_timeout.py is WIRED, called by the live host, and its rejected sidecar was separately proven debris because the canonical version was AHEAD of it, rounding the support price up one tick where the rejected copy used the bare support; willkim_realtime_***.py and its selftest are the PRODUCTION HOST itself, so calling the host unwired is a category error, and its one genuinely open seam is floor_pct, which needs an owner decision on the value and must land net-zero because the host is 2039 lines under fat-source-growth. THE RULE: the wish counter scores FILES TOUCHED BY A COMMIT THIS SESSION, not wiring, so a file wired months ago stays on the STILL UNWIRED list forever and every successor re-chases it. A wish list is INHERITED, never measured -- disprove it with a call-site grep before spending a single dispatch on it, and a disproof closes a wish exactly as a fix does. Cross: wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring ; wkappbot skill read wk-unwired

SPEC, owner directive 2026-09-13: INSTRUMENT Block ITSELF, because that is the ONLY moment all three facts exist together -- WHICH guard refused, WHAT it refused, and WHICH file the newest ledger entry opened. Today only the third is printed and the other two are discarded where they stand. THE DEFECT, observed continuously across a ten-hour session and visible in one verbatim pair: emergency-edit GRANTED wkharness-guards-onload-enforce-demix.ps1 is now editable, immediately followed by forced-study BLOCKED naming five skills. The opened file has no stated relation to the thing refused, so the grant reads as noise and the session routes around the block instead of repairing it. THE SAME FILE WAS GRANTED REPEATEDLY with byte-identical wording and no ordinal, so a session never learns it is ALREADY HOLDING the permission it needs. THREE ADDITIONS where Block composes its message. ONE, NAME THE BLOCKER: this refusal came from guardsource at line N, and that file is editable now, so repair it there if the block is unjust. TWO, THE OWNER'S SPECIFIC CASE, DETECT THE MATCH: when the newest ledger entry names the SAME source that just raised this refusal, say so outright instead of printing the generic grant -- you already hold the permission to fix the guard refusing you. THREE, TWO LEDGER RULES THE WRITER DOES NOT HAVE, both owner directives, and READ VERIFIED IN Add-WkEmergencyEditEntry at lines 160 to 184: it calls AppendAllText and nothing else -- no creation-time check, no session comparison, no dedupe. RULE A, CLEAR A STALE LIST BEFORE WRITING: if the list file was created BEFORE this session started, delete it and begin fresh. Today it is one growing file per repo, so a guard stamped in a PREVIOUS session still sits in the reachable tail and opens a file for a session that never met that block. The module header claims a new entry pushes the oldest out of reach, and that is true only WITHIN a session -- after a quiet session yesterday's entries are still at the bottom. RULE B, DEDUPE, which supersedes the ordinal idea this step first carried. A source ALREADY on the list is NEVER re-added: say already open rather than writing a new entry. THE REACHABLE WINDOW MUST HOLD DISTINCT SOURCE LOCATIONS, so the last three entries are three DIFFERENT files. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE WORDING: step 4 keeps only the last few entries reachable so permission cannot accumulate, and a file that re-stamps on every refusal FILLS THAT WINDOW BY ITSELF and evicts every other repair grant -- measured across a ten-hour session, one hub file took nearly every slot while unrelated guards that had also refused were pushed out unreachable. Dedupe turns a window of N slots into N genuinely different repairs, and it deletes the ordinal problem instead of reporting it. THE PART THAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND STILL UNWIRED IS THE PART THIS NEEDS: step 8 of this skill closes by saying Get-WkBlockingGuardSource.ps1 landed from a sector, not run, no cases, no call site checked -- and its own header states the intent, open the guard that blocked you instead of the file you were trying to write. So the resolver exists, the door exists, and nothing joins them. RUN ITS REFUSAL CASES FIRST, then wire it into Block. ON PRINTING A SLOW-MARK DETECTION TOO, asked the same day and the answer is DO NOT ADD A CHANNEL: a slow verdict is only available at FLUSH, after the hook has finished, while a Block message is composed mid-hook, so this run's verdict does not yet exist when the refusal fires; and on a hook measured at 4503 ms almost every span crosses a 1000 ms threshold, so it would print on nearly every call -- the exact noise the owner's bundle-every-reason directive exists to remove. THE VERSION THAT DOES NOT TANGLE: the tracer ALREADY auto-registers a source over threshold onto the repair list, so make the EXISTING grant line state WHY it was opened -- opened because it BLOCKED you, or opened because it MEASURED N ms -- which costs no new channel and turns one line into a diagnosis. FAIL DIRECTION FOR ALL OF IT: every addition is text appended to a refusal already in flight, so an unresolvable stack or unreadable ledger falls through to today's exact wording and can never turn a refusal into an allow. VERIFY BY WHAT IT STILL REFUSES: provoke a real block twice on the same guard and read the SECOND message for the ordinal, then provoke one on a DIFFERENT guard and confirm the match line is absent.

BUG (2026-09-22): emergency-write-freeze fires BEFORE the emergency edit door can grant access. When agy-sandbox blocks a command with Block(), the guard source file is stamped for repair, but emergency-write-freeze intercepts the repair attempt with a model-grade check (non-pro rejected) before the door can open. This means the emergency edit door is DEAD for AGY non-pro sessions on canonical source. The fix should either: (a) exempt stamped repair targets from write-freeze, or (b) reorder the guards so the door check runs before write-freeze.

IMPLEMENTATION RULE (2026-09-22): The emergency edit door must be wired immediately after harness initialization, mimicking the Claude family implementation (e.g., tools/wkharness-claude-main.ps1). This ensures it evaluates BEFORE emergency-write-freeze and avoids deadlocks for non-pro models.
